text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Edgar Bronfman, President of the World Jewish Congress, said he was satisfied with Switzerland's plan to set up a Solidarity Foundation following a meeting with Swiss foreign minister Flavio Cotti, who is on a three-day visit to the U.S. - Michael Ringier, head of Ringier, Switzerland's biggest publishing house, will assume the position of chief operating officer in April. - Crypto AG in Steinhausen in the canton of Zug, will cut 40 jobs as part of a restructuring programme. - Bank fuer Handel und Effekten posted a profit rise of 1.1 million Swiss francs to 14.1 million for 1996. TAGES ANZEIGER - Zurich's Evangelist-Reformed church said it will give one million Swiss francs to the Jewish Historical Foundation to help in the safe-keeping of hundreds of files it has stored on Jewish and non-Jewish refugees. - Uniphase Corporation, a U.S. firm based in California, took over IBM's Laser Enterprise in Zurich. - Touring Club Schweiz and Imholz Travel Group signed a contract to cooperate. - Economists in Basle predict one percent growth in Switzerland's Gross Domestic Product for 1997. - Sulzer Technology Group sold Sulzer Thermtec for 30 million Swiss francs to British engineering group IMI. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Switzerland named 56-year-old diplomat Jacques Reverdin, currently a director at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in London, as the new Swiss Consul General in New York. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
